key_findings: **FULL 36-CLASS REGISTRY ENUMERATED** (had estimated ~30; actual count is 36). Two registration styles split at class id 11/12 boundary: classes 0-11 (12 classes) use FUN_00CC71F0 (LGTC-style: Global, Debug, Math, String, Table, WorldMaster, OtherArea, SpreadSheet, CutScene, CommandDebuggerGM/DEV/TEST); classes 12-35 (24 classes) use FUN_00CC71E0 (BaseClass-style: SystemBaseClass, ProgDebugBaseClass, ActorBaseClass, CharaBaseClass, PlayerBaseClass, NpcBaseClass, WorldBaseClass, AreaBaseClass, PrivateAreaBaseClass, ZoneBaseClass, DebugBaseClass, JudgeBaseClass, CommandBaseClass, StatusBaseClass, QuestBaseClass, DirectorBaseClass, CommandDebuggerBaseClass, CommandDebuggerFUNCBaseClass, ItemBaseClass, ImportantItemBaseClass, MoneyItemBaseClass, NormalItemBaseClass, GameDataBaseClass, GroupBaseClass).

**23 of 36 registry classes have catalog matches** (some via direct TDs, others via tangentially-related entries). Cataloged with strong TD presence: Global (BCS-Y-1592), Math (BCS-Y-1591), String (BCS-Y-1596), Table (BCS-Y-1597), CutScene (per BCS-Y-1473 ctor), CharaBaseClass (BCS-Y-1721 NEW), StatusBaseClass (BCS-Y-1497), QuestBaseClass (BCS-Y-1595), CommandBaseClass (BCS-Y-1593), JudgeBaseClass (BCS-Y-1594), GroupBaseClass (BCS-Y-1588), ItemBaseClass (BCS-Y-1589). Plus 11 others with partial matches (Debug, WorldMaster, SpreadSheet, ActorBaseClass, PlayerBaseClass, NpcBaseClass, AreaBaseClass, PrivateAreaBaseClass, DebugBaseClass, DirectorBaseClass, CommandDebuggerBaseClass).

**13 GAP CLASSES** (registered in FUN_0078E3A0 but NO catalog presence): OtherArea (id 6), CommandDebuggerGM (id 9), CommandDebuggerDEV (id 10), CommandDebuggerTEST (id 11), SystemBaseClass (id 12), ProgDebugBaseClass (id 13), WorldBaseClass (id 18), ZoneBaseClass (id 21), CommandDebuggerFUNCBaseClass (id 29), ImportantItemBaseClass (id 31), MoneyItemBaseClass (id 32), NormalItemBaseClass (id 33), GameDataBaseClass (id 34).

**THE 13 GAPS ARE ABSTRACT LUA-BRIDGE BASES, NOT CATALOG OMISSIONS**. Grep of `manifests/rtti_extraction_OUR.txt` (RTTI ground truth, all class TDs extracted from the binary) returned ZERO matches for any of the 13 GAP names. This means the GAP classes have NO C++ class TD in the binary - they exist ONLY as registry entries. Architectural interpretation: these are 'abstract base' classes that Lua scripts use to declare derived classes via `_defineClass` / `_defineBaseClass` (per client-architecture 'The LGE class system is a 5-userdata-type model' / class registry bridge). The C++ engine registers them as named slots in the LGE class table so that Lua code can reference them as parent classes, but no C++ implementation exists for them.

**LGTC vs BaseClass split is at id 11/12 (not 3/4 as the implied)**. The first 12 classes (LGTC-style via FUN_00CC71F0) are concrete classes with C++ implementations. The next 24 classes (BaseClass-style via FUN_00CC71E0) include both concrete classes (ActorBase, CharaBase, PlayerBase, NpcBase, StatusBase, etc.) AND abstract Lua-bridge bases (SystemBaseClass, WorldBaseClass, ZoneBaseClass, etc.). So 'BaseClass-style' registration doesn't imply 'no C++ impl' - it's just a different registration mechanism.

**FOUR distinct CommandDebugger entries** (none of the 4 are cataloged): CommandDebuggerGM (id 9, LGTC), CommandDebuggerDEV (id 10, LGTC), CommandDebuggerTEST (id 11, LGTC), CommandDebuggerBaseClass (id 28, BaseClass), CommandDebuggerFUNCBaseClass (id 29, BaseClass). Suggests a debug-mode subsystem with 3 user-mode variants (GM/DEV/TEST) + 2 base classes - likely Lua-scriptable debug commands restricted by user role. The 3 user-mode variants (GM/DEV/TEST) are real classes (LGTC concrete) but happen to be uncataloged - they could be enumerable via Ghidra symbol scan of `Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::CommandDebugger*` namespace. Deferred follow-up.

**FOUR distinct *ItemBaseClass variants** (3 of 4 are GAP): ItemBaseClass (id 30, cataloged BCS-Y-1589), ImportantItemBaseClass (id 31, GAP), MoneyItemBaseClass (id 32, GAP), NormalItemBaseClass (id 33, GAP). The 3 GAPs are likely abstract Lua-bridge bases for item categories (Important/Money/Normal). Lua scripts probably declare specific items inheriting from these abstract bases, and the C++ engine routes them to the concrete ItemBase implementation.
